messages:
Alicia M.: Hey team — hit a tricky one. My partner had an emergency and I need to take 3 days starting tomorrow. I haven’t formally started my parental leave yet (planning to in 2 months). What’s the quickest way to get short-term coverage and make sure payroll reflects this?

David (Eng Manager): Alicia — sorry to hear that, hope all ok. For immediate coverage we usually ask for: 1) swap-oncall if applicable, 2) post a short handoff in the team channel, 3) request temp contractor backfill if >3 days. @People Ops can confirm the expedite path.

People Ops - Priya: Alicia, sending hugs. For an unplanned short absence we have two parallel paths: Paid Emergency Dependent Care (EDC) stipend request and ad-hoc PTO conversion. Steps: 1) file the Emergency Leave form (link below) within 72h, 2) mark your time as PTO in Workday, 3) if you need >5 business days, we trigger coverage/backfill. EDC is for care-related emergencies up to 5 days.

People Ops - Priya: Link to form: https://hr.redwood.example.com/emergency-care-form (internal) — please fill and attach any docs if available. If you’d like, I can pre-fill the form with what you give me and submit on your behalf.

Alicia M.: Thanks Priya — yes please can you pre-fill? I’ll DM you the details. Quick Q: does EDC pay out immediately or through payroll next cycle?

Payroll Bot: Alicia M.: Emergency Dependent Care stipend requests submitted before payroll lock will be included in the next pay cycle; otherwise processed in the subsequent cycle. Typical turnaround: 1 payroll cycle after approval.

Michelle HR: To add — if you need to keep some time unpaid so you don’t burn parental leave bank, we can set up unpaid leave. But EDC is usually cleaner for short emergencies. Also remind managers to update the oncall schedule and tag any customer-critical tickets for handoff.

Raj (Eng Lead): Alicia, if you want I can take your oncall for the 3 days. Also drop a 1-paragraph handoff here and I’ll post in eng-oncall. Example handoff snippet:

```
Handoff: Alicia M. covering absent 3/soon - primary contact Raj (eng lead). Key in-progress: #1234 regression in ranking-service (PR open: https://...); oauth renewal scheduled 03/15 — no action needed until return; blocked: infra deploy waiting on infra-ops review (ticket #987). Pager: high for production errors; Slack channel #eng-oncall.
```

Alicia M.: Raj — massive thank you, please do. Priya — DMing now. One more: will this emergency time impact my accruals or parental leave start date?

People Ops - Priya: Short absences covered by EDC/pTO do not shift your approved parental leave start date. If you later request to move your parental leave start, we’ll treat it as a separate request and handle payroll accruals accordingly. Accruals: up to company policy — short EDC days are paid and do not reduce accruals.

David (Eng Manager): Also flagging that if you need extended coverage we have a temporary backfill budget you can request; we'll fast-track approvals for urgent caregiver cases.

Alicia M.: All right — that helps. Appreciate everyone being flexible. Priya — let me know once the form is submitted.

People Ops - Priya: Form received via DM — I’ve pre-filled and submitted on your behalf. Case ID: EDC-2026-459. Payroll will confirm inclusion in the next cycle. I’ve also notified Eng Ops to post a contractor request if more than 5 days are needed. :heart:

Payroll Bot: Payroll system: case EDC-2026-459 logged. Status: pending approval. Next update expected within 24 hours.

Alicia M.: Perfect — thank you all. Will post a short handoff in 10m and set status in Workday.

Raj (Eng Lead): Ping me if anything urgent comes up, I’ve got your inbox and pager. :thumbsup:
